extra_misconceptions.fact: Megawatts measure instantaneous power capacity, whereas megawatt-hours measure actual energy generated over a specific time period.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Media articles that report power plant capacity in megawatts are stating the exact amount of electricity delivered every hour.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Requirement 1b requires re-evaluating the exact same article from 1a using the technical concepts learned in requirements 2 through 8.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Completing requirement 1b means finding a brand-new article on energy conservation at the end of the merit badge.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Conservation reduces energy use through behavior changes, while efficiency uses technology to perform the same work with less energy.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Energy conservation and energy efficiency mean the exact same thing when authors discuss reducing utility bills.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Popular blogs often omit capacity factors and lifecycle costs, so Scouts should cross-check claims against EIA or DOE data.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Any blog or podcast about renewable energy provides peer-reviewed engineering data suitable for technical analysis.

extra_socratic_questions: What changes in your analysis when you revisit your original energy article after completing requirements two through eight?
Which unit distinction separates power output in kilowatts from total energy consumption in kilowatt-hours inside an article?
What specific source metadata and quantitative claims should you record in your notebook before discussing the article?
Why is it necessary to obtain parent or guardian permission and verify domain credibility before researching energy media online?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Nichrome heating elements convert electrical energy into thermal and infrared radiant energy, which then drives surface browning.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A toaster converts electrical energy directly into chemical energy without producing any radiant or thermal energy.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Batteries store chemical potential energy and convert it into electrical energy through electrochemical reactions during discharge.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: An electric vehicle battery stores pure electrical energy in its cells until the driver presses the accelerator pedal.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Nuclear fission releases thermal energy to boil water into high-pressure steam, which spins a mechanical turbine and generator.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A nuclear reactor generates electricity directly from splitting uranium atoms inside the reactor core without a turbine.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Regenerative braking converts a portion of the vehicle's kinetic energy back into electrical and chemical energy in the battery.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Regenerative braking in an electric vehicle creates brand-new energy that did not exist in the vehicle system before.

extra_socratic_questions: What sequence of energy forms occurs at each stage of the multi-conversion system you constructed for requirement 2b?
Under what physical mechanism does a greenhouse trap long-wave infrared thermal energy after short-wave light passes through glass?
Which observable physical indicator confirms that each energy conversion stage in your homemade device actually transferred energy?
Why is it dangerous to test a bow drill or resistance heating element indoors without eye protection and a heatproof base?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Lost energy is never destroyed; it converts into low-grade thermal energy, sound, or vibration that cannot do useful work.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Energy losses in a mechanical or electrical system mean that a portion of the energy is permanently destroyed and ceases to exist.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Every real thermodynamic cycle rejects some waste heat to its surroundings, making one hundred percent efficiency physically impossible.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Lubricating bearings and insulating pipes can raise a real heat engine's thermal efficiency all the way to one hundred percent.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Incandescent bulbs convert roughly ninety percent of their electrical energy into waste heat and only ten percent into visible light.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: An incandescent lightbulb is primarily a lighting device that converts most of its electrical input into visible light.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Electricity is an energy carrier; the primary energy source is the coal, natural gas, nuclear fuel, or renewables at the power plant.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: The primary source of energy for an electric home furnace is the wall outlet or breaker panel inside the house.

extra_socratic_questions: Where along your chosen system's component pathway does the largest fraction of input energy escape as waste heat or friction?
What thermodynamic principle explains why total energy stays constant even while usable energy decreases across every system stage?
What measurement confirms the percentage efficiency of a system when you compare useful energy output against total energy input?
Why should you use a non-contact infrared thermometer rather than bare hands when locating waste heat losses on a running motor?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Devices in standby mode continue drawing phantom power continuously until unplugged or switched off at a controlled power strip.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Turning a television or gaming console off with the remote control stops all electrical power draw from the wall outlet.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Most home furnaces deliver heat at a constant rate, so a higher thermostat setting only causes the system to overshoot and waste fuel.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Cranking a home thermostat to eighty-five degrees heats a cold house faster than setting it to the desired seventy degrees.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Gas meters measure volume in hundred cubic feet, which the utility converts into therms based on the heating value of the gas.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Residential natural gas meters measure fuel consumption directly in kilowatt-hours just like an electric utility meter.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Closing too many registers increases duct static pressure, restricts blower airflow, and can reduce furnace and heat pump efficiency.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Closing supply vents in unused rooms always lowers central forced-air furnace energy consumption during a two-week home audit.

extra_socratic_questions: What baseline utility meter or odometer readings must you record on day one so your 14-day conservation log shows real savings?
Which units on a utility bill distinguish natural gas volume in CCF from heat content in therms and electricity in kWh?
Where should a Scout position a draft detector or plug-in wattmeter to uncover hidden air leaks and standby phantom loads at home?
Why is it dangerous to inspect a natural gas furnace, water heater flue, or main electrical panel without adult supervision?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Modern LED and fluorescent fixtures draw only a fraction of a second of inrush current, so turning them off always saves electricity.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Leaving fluorescent or LED classroom lights on all afternoon uses less electricity than turning them off and back on between classes.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Idling for more than ten seconds consumes more fuel and emits more exhaust pollutants than shutting off and restarting a warm engine.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Idling a car or school bus engine for ten minutes in a pickup lane uses less fuel than restarting a warm engine.

extra_misconceptions.fact: People often resist energy changes because of high upfront equipment costs, disrupted daily routines, or perceived loss of comfort.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Energy conservation proposals fail in communities only because residents do not care about lowering utility costs or pollution.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Sound energy trade-offs weigh upfront capital expense, embodied manufacturing energy, and payback time against ongoing energy savings.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Replacing every municipal streetlight or HVAC unit immediately is always the best choice regardless of remaining equipment life.

extra_socratic_questions: What operating schedules and conditions should you record in your notebook for each of the five community energy waste sites?
Under what condition does an energy-saving retrofit create a trade-off between upfront capital cost, convenience, and payback time?
What calculation links wasted operating hours of school lighting or idling vehicles to annual dollar cost and carbon emissions?
Why must Scouts observe school and municipal energy systems from public areas rather than opening locked mechanical rooms?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Total primary energy includes petroleum used directly for transportation, whereas electricity generation relies mainly on gas and coal.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: The pie chart for U.S. electricity generation fuels is identical to the pie chart for total U.S. primary energy consumption.

extra_misconceptions.fact: The industrial and transportation sectors each consume a larger share of total U.S. primary energy than residential households.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Residential homes consume a larger share of total United States energy than the industrial, commercial, or transportation sectors.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Proven reserves count only the fraction of known deposits that can be extracted economically with current technology and fuel prices.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Known proven energy reserves represent the exact total physical amount of fossil fuel remaining inside the Earth's crust.

extra_misconceptions.fact: As easy deposits deplete, rising extraction and environmental costs make renewable alternatives cost-competitive long before exhaustion.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A society switches from a nonrenewable fuel to alternatives only after the physical supply of the resource is completely gone.

extra_socratic_questions: What verification steps ensure that your five energy pie charts sum to one hundred percent and cite current EIA or IEA data?
What distinction separates total U.S. primary energy consumption in chart 6a from the electricity generation fuel mix in chart 6d?
Which common energy unit allows you to normalize barrels of oil, cubic feet of gas, and kilowatt-hours before plotting a pie chart?
Why does rising extraction cost for depleted nonrenewable reserves make renewable alternatives economically practical over time?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Cogeneration captures exhaust heat from electricity generation to heat buildings or industrial processes, raising overall efficiency.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Cogeneration plants generate extra electricity out of nothing by violating the law of conservation of energy.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Fuel cells convert chemical energy from hydrogen and oxygen directly into DC electricity and water through an electrochemical membrane.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Hydrogen fuel cells burn hydrogen gas in an open flame to spin a miniature mechanical turbine and electrical generator.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Utility-scale geothermal power requires high-temperature subsurface rock or hydrothermal reservoirs and careful reinjection management.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Geothermal power plants can operate at high efficiency anywhere on Earth by drilling a shallow well into ordinary topsoil.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Solar and wind produce zero operating emissions, but require mineral mining, land use planning, fall protection, and battery recycling.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Solar photovoltaic panels and wind turbines have zero environmental impacts or safety hazards across their entire lifecycle.

extra_socratic_questions: What four evaluation criteria must you compare across each of the five power generation technologies you select for requirement 7?
What engineering mechanism allows a cogeneration plant to capture and use thermal energy that a conventional power plant rejects?
Which performance metric shows whether taller wind turbine towers or solar trackers actually increase annual usable energy output?
Why do anaerobic biomass digesters and hydrogen fuel cell systems require continuous gas leak detection and explosion-proof venting?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Skilled energy trades such as wind technicians, solar installers, and power lineworkers often enter through paid apprenticeships.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Every career in the energy sector requires a four-year university engineering degree and carries heavy student loan debt.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Earning a Professional Engineer license requires passing the FE exam, completing years of supervised work, and passing the PE exam.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Graduating with a bachelor's degree in engineering immediately grants a legally recognized Professional Engineer license.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Grid modernization, industrial decarbonization, and stricter building codes continue driving strong demand for energy auditors.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Careers in energy efficiency and building auditing are disappearing as renewable power generation expands across the grid.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Strict electrical, high-voltage, and hazardous-energy safety certifications are mandatory for every field technician and engineer.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Safety certifications in power generation and transmission are optional credentials completed only by site supervisors.

extra_socratic_questions: Which accredited labor databases and professional societies provide verified data on training expenses, salaries, and job prospects?
What credential requirements distinguish a licensed Professional Engineer from a Certified Energy Manager or lineworker apprentice?
What financial comparison helps you evaluate whether a degree or apprenticeship's training expenses match its starting salary?
Why do energy sector employers require lock-out/tag-out and arc-flash safety training before technicians work on live equipment?
